propositions: The current clarity measure awards points for volume and legacy type-specific shape rather than enforcing the author guide's leaf/container contract and required-section structure.
Clarity-score computation is duplicated across gates.py and det_floor.py, creating maintenance drift; the deterministic floor lacks a bug branch present in the gates implementation.

Documented plan-writing guidance and current deterministic clarity checks diverge on required sections, Success Criteria vs. Acceptance Criteria naming, and rejected-alternative requirements, preventing reliable overlap detection.

Seven mechanically testable additions are proposed (required-section shape by graph altitude, AC verification coverage, placeholder detection, structured file_impact, AC hygiene, Testing shape markers, and LLM-reserved semantic judgments) to replace length/bullet-point padding.
Deriving compatibility score from satisfied/applicable checks instead of additive points would prevent filler from masking missing required sections.
